messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Teams: Registration capacity for town halls and webinars increases to 20,000
messageCenterItems.summary: Starting December 2026, Microsoft Teams town halls and webinars registration capacity scales with attendee limits, up to 20,000 registrations per event. Teams Enterprise allows 3,000; Attendee Capacity Packs allow up to 20,000. Rollout occurs from mid-December 2026 to late January 2027. No action required.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 23, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

What and why

Starting in December, registration capacity for Microsoft Teams town halls and webinars scales with the event's attendee capacity, up to 20,000 registrations per event. Organizers with Teams Enterprise can allow up to 3,000 registrations. Organizers with Attendee Capacity Packs can allow up to 20,000. Organizers can use this to plan large-scale events with registration.

Rollout schedule

  • Public Preview: We will begin rolling out on mid-December 2026 and expect to complete by late December 2026.
  • General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in early January 2027 and expect to complete by late January 2027.

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Organizers of Teams town halls and webinars that use registration
  • Admins who manage Teams events policies and Attendee Capacity Pack licenses

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams (town halls and webinars)

What will happen

  • Registration capacity scales with attendee capacity, up to 20,000 registrations per event.
  • Organizers with Teams Enterprise can allow up to 3,000 registrations.
  • Organizers with Attendee Capacity Packs can allow up to 20,000 registrations.
  • Large webinars with registration don't support broadcast-style streaming, which is available with town halls.
  • Organizers still need the right events policy. No new policy access is needed, only the right Attendee Capacity Pack where applicable.
  • Existing Teams events policies and admin controls don't change.
  • We plan to support more registrations per event in future releases.

Action required and recommendations

No action is required. To prepare, you can:

  • Tell organizers about the higher registration limits.
  • Make sure organizers who need more than 3,000 registrations per event have an Attendee Capacity Pack of the right size. Assign packs in the Teams admin center (Add-on Licenses > Teams Events).
  • Update internal training and documentation that mention a 1,000-registration limit.
  • Review your Teams events policies in the Teams admin center (Meetings > Events policies) to confirm they meet your organization's needs.

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

messageCenterItems.title: New VDI solution for Omnissa on Mac
messageCenterItems.summary: A new VDI optimization for Omnissa on Mac using a SlimCore-based media engine will enhance Microsoft Teams' quality, reliability, and performance. Rollout starts December 2026 to February 2027. Upgrade Horizon Client (2609.1+) and Teams (26304.1207.5384.858+) to benefit. No compliance issues noted.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and Why:

New VDI optimization for Omnissa on Mac. This feature allows Mac endpoints to optimize Microsoft Teams in VDI environments with the new SlimCore-based media engine, providing an expanded feature set and multiple improvements in quality, reliability and performance.

Rollout Schedule:

Global: We will begin rolling out on early December 2026 and expect to complete by early February 2027.

Impact on Your Organization:

With this release, a new media engine delivers a better user experience that is aligned with the rich feature set and performance native Mac Teams users have.

Action Required/Recommendations:

Upgrade your Horizon Client for Mac to an upcoming release (2609.1 or higher). Upgrade Teams to 26304.1207.5384.858 or higher.

Compliance considerations:

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Teams: Updated recording and transcript access setting behavior for town halls and webinars
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Teams is updating the "Who has access to the recording or transcript" option for Events App town halls and webinars. Starting mid-January 2027, access will depend on the RecordingForTownhall or RecordingForWebinar settings, not AllowCloudRecording. No action is required.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 23, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

What and why

We are updating how the Who has access to the recording or transcript option appears for Microsoft Teams Events scheduling through the Events App including town halls and webinars. Currently, when AllowCloudRecording is set to false, this option does not appear for these events. After this change, the option will appear only when the applicable RecordingForTownhall or RecordingForWebinar setting in CsTeamsEventsPolicy is enabled.

Rollout schedule

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Beginning in mid-January 2027 (previously early-November 2026) and expected to complete by late January 2027 (previously mid-November 2026)

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Microsoft Teams organizers of Events created via the Events App including town halls and webinars

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft TeamsEvents created via the Events App including town halls and webinars

What will happen

The Who has access to the recording or transcript option will be based on the applicable RecordingForTownhall or RecordingForWebinar setting. It will no longer be based on the AllowCloudRecording setting.

Action required and recommendations

No action is required to enable this change.

We recommend updating your internal documentation to reflect this change.

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.
